put.summary: Turn the analyst on or off and choose its provider and model

400.description: Invalid input or service not configured

403.description: Only a platform administrator may use this

502.description: The assistant provider could not be reached

put.description: Applies to the whole deployment, to the next question; turning it off also stops questions already being answered. A model is only accepted from the chosen provider's own list, which needs a key for that provider (saved here, or set in the server environment); switching off is always accepted. `dailyTokenLimit`, when given, must be at least what one question reserves.

model.description: The provider's model id, one it lists. May be empty only while turning the analyst off.

dailyTokenLimit.description: Tokens per person per day. Must cover one question at the chosen toolRounds, including the screen allowance. Left out, it stays as it is.

toolRounds.description: Rounds per answer; defaults to 8, omitted preserves the saved value.

400.description: Invalid input or service not configured

get.description: The chat models available to the server's key for that provider (the one in use when none is named), newest first. The newest model of each plain kind is marked with its `tier` (`best`, `balanced`, `fast`), and `recommended` names the one to start with, so a model can be chosen without knowing model names. `reachable` is false when they could not be listed, for instance because there is no key yet. Callers asking at the same moment share one request to the provider.

get.summary: Read what the analyst has used, and what that costs

400.description: Invalid input or service not configured

403.description: Only a platform administrator may use this

502.description: The assistant provider could not be reached

get.description: Administrators only. Answered questions in the last `days` UTC days (1 to 365, default 30; today counts as a day): their tokens in total and by day, model and person, and what they cost. Each question is costed at the price that was kept with it when it was answered, so a price changed later affects only later questions; `byModel[].pricesInPeriod` says when the questions of a model were asked at more than one price. A question asked before its model had a price has none and shows tokens only (`unpricedQuestions`, `unpricedTokens`) until an administrator prices it afterwards (POST /settings/assistant/prices/backfill), after which it is counted in `backfilledQuestions`. Where the prices in the period are in more than one currency `currency` is `MIXED` and there is no cost total. Only completed answers count, because only they report their tokens; `failedQuestions` says how many others did not finish. Cost is an estimate from token counts and those prices, not an invoice. `byModel[].price` is the price a question asked now would be costed at, and `prices` is every price entered, so the editor can send them back. Input token totals include ordinary, cache-read and cache-write tokens exactly once. Optional cacheReadPerMillion and cacheWritePerMillion rates are saved with each run; a missing applicable rate leaves that question unpriced. performance reports cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, providerRequests, toolCalls and total durationMs for completed questions. performance.measuredQuestions counts timed answers, so legacy records are excluded from average latency.

400.description: Invalid input or service not configured

403.description: Only a platform administrator may use this

put.description: Administrators only. Replaces the whole price table: a price is removed by leaving it out. Prices are per million input and output tokens, in one currency for the deployment, and apply to questions answered from then on: a question keeps the price it was asked at. Providers return no price with an answer and change prices, so none is built in.

currency.description: A three-letter currency code, such as USD. Stored upper-cased.

source.description: Typed by an administrator, which a refresh never overwrites, or fetched from the price list. Sent back as received so a fetched price stays marked until it is edited.

fetchedAt.description: When a fetched price was fetched.

cacheReadPerMillion.description: Optional model-specific cache price per million tokens. A cached question without the applicable rate remains unpriced.

cacheWritePerMillion.description: Optional model-specific cache price per million tokens. A cached question without the applicable rate remains unpriced.

post.summary: Fetch current prices from the price list

400.description: Invalid input or service not configured

403.description: Only a platform administrator may use this

post.description: Administrators only. Fetches LiteLLM's public price list and sets a fetched price for every model that has answered a question and every model already in the table as fetched. A price typed by an administrator is never overwritten. The list is in USD, so this is refused when the deployment's currency is another. Nothing changes unless the list was read in full: a failed fetch returns 502 and the prices stay as they were. The response is the price table plus a `refresh` summary: `updated`, `notFound` (no usable price in the list), `keptManual`, and `fetchedAt`.

post.summary: Price earlier questions that have no price

400.description: Invalid input or service not configured

403.description: Only a platform administrator may use this

post.description: Administrators only. Prices answered questions that were asked before their model had a price, at the price in the table now, and marks each as backfilled. It is an estimate (the price then may have been different) and is never done on its own. Questions that already have a price are left exactly as they are, so repeating it changes nothing. Returns how many questions were priced, by model. Also fills missing applicable cache rates for previously priced questions in the same currency, retaining their original input/output prices and any existing cache prices. Such additions are marked as backfilled estimates.

put.summary: Save the deployment key for a provider

400.description: Invalid input or service not configured

403.description: Only a platform administrator may use this

502.description: The assistant provider could not be reached

put.description: Administrators only. The key is checked with the provider before it is kept, then stored encrypted with API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_SECRET (which must be set). It replaces any key saved before and is never returned: the settings only say where a key came from and show a saved key's last four characters. A saved key is used instead of one set in the server environment.

key.description: The provider's API key. Never returned by any route.
